This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.164 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 28.01.2024 at about 12.30 a.m. he had been riding Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53- SCCH-5 HK-8429 near Arkavathi Bridge, Makali,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru - Tumkur Road, NH-4, Bengaluru, at that time, he lost control over the motor cycle and fell down, as a result he has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Abhay Vasishta Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein firstaid treatment was given, thereafter shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for the medical expenses he has spent a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- towards medical, food, conveyance and other charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 23 years, hale and healthy, he was doing 5 years law course in V.V.Puram Law College, Bengaluru and also doing internship in Bharani Law Associates,
thereby drawing salary of Rs.3,300/- p.m.
Due to the accidental SCCH-5 injuries, he could not attend his college along with court and he could not attend the examination due.
Out of this accident crime No.35/2024 is registered before the Nelamangala Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-HK-8429 they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 being the owner of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-HK-8429 and respondent No.2 being the insurer have remained absent, hence respondent No.1 and 2 are placed exparte.
5. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself has deposed his evidence as PW-1 and marked SCCH-5 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents, as they have placed exparte.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record,
7.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, the following points that would arise for my consideration:
Nishchal More N vs Girish B L on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56601727/
2 ::POINTS::
1.

sentences.text:
Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.01.2024 at about 12.30 a.m. when he was riding Yamaha motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-HK-8429 near Arkavathi Bridge,
Makali, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru - Tumkur Road, NH-4, Bengaluru due to use of the motor cycle bnrKA-53-HK- 8429, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH-5 2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

8. Then my findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
9. Point No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of SCCH-5 charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7.
10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, charge sheet, mahazar, Sec.133 notice, reply and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 28.01.2024 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, inspite of issuance of summons respondents have remained absent and have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the SCCH-5 petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 28.01.2024 at about 12.30 a.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-HK-8429 near Arkavathi Bridge, Makali, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru - Tumkur Road,
NH-4, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.

sentences.text: The police papers speaks about filing of charge sheet against the petitioner, that too this petition has filed by the petitioner under Sec.164 of M.V.Act, hence he is entitled for compensation as per the said provisions.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the SCCH-5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Point No.1 in the affirmative.

13. Point No.2:- As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 23 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.13, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 02.10.2000 and the alleged accident was occurred on 28.01.2024, accordingly relying on Ex.P.13 his age is considered about 24 years as on the date of accident.

Further it is the case of the petitioner that, he was studying 5 year law course in V.V.Puram Law College and also doing internship in Bharani Law Associates, Cubbonpet, Bengaluru, thereby earning a sum of Rs.3,300/- p.m.
To prove the same, he has not exhibited any income proof documents.
SCCH-5 14.

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained severe head injury, right fronto - parieto - temporal SDH with midline shaft, bilateral basifrontal and right temporal multiple hemorrhagic contusion, bilateral frontal SAH, multiple facial bone fracture.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by Sparsh Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient since 28.01.2024 to 08.02.2024 and also from 22.04.2024 to 26.04.2024 i.e., for 15 days.

Petitioner has also exhibited medical bills amounting to Rs.18,75,610/- marked as Ex.P.11.
15.
Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated him nor produced the disability certificate towards the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.8 in which Doctor SCCH-5 who have treated i.e., Dr.Prani has categorically stated that,
petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 28.01.2024.
So as per Ex.P.8 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained lacerated wound on the forehead, which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Nischal N. More for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
16.
Further petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills to the tune of Rs.18,75,610/-.
On perusal of the said bills, Sl.No.5 is the calculation sheet for Rs.1,59,083/-, but to prove the said amount, there are SCCH-5 no separate bills are exhibited by the petitioner.
Further petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.14 i.e., advance receipts, which cannot be considered for calculation of total medical bills.

So considering Sl.No.1 for Rs.4,14,032/-, Sl.No.3 for Rs.6,88,073/- and Sl.No.6 to 10 for Rs.9,723/-, in total Rs.11,11,828/- for the said amount, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in the head of medical expenses.
17. This petition is filed under Sec.164 of M.V.Act.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- along with medical expenses of Rs.11,11,828/-, totally a sum of Nishchal More N vs Girish B L on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56601727/
4 Rs.13,61,828/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

sentences.text: 18. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing SCCH-5 No.201250020121801837700000 valid from 09.03.2022 to 08.03.2027, the alleged accident was occurred on 28.01.2024 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that,
respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Point No.2 partly in the affirmative.

19. Point No.3: For the reasons assigned to Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,61,828/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Sixty One Thousand Eight Hundred Twenty Eight SCCH-5 Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 7th day of February, 2025)

(MANJUNATHA K.P.)
VIII ADDL.
JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES & ACJM, BENGALURU.
